This means w could be a possible fallback. I have priority 2 at both x and z. Given the general applicant preference for y > x > w > z, x is likely to be more competitive than z. Therefore, x is a possible fallback.

Thus, my obtainable schools are likely to be {y, w, x, z}. It's highly probable I get y if I rank it first. If y is full, my priority at w is 1, so w is the next best option. If w is full, my priority at x is 2, so x is next. Finally, z.

Because my ranking doesn't affect *which* schools are obtainable, I should simply rank them according to my *preference* order. This will ensure I get my highest-ranked school *from* the set of obtainable schools.
